optimized.method: geometry-only: drop original NORMAL, weld by position, meshoptimizer simplify (Prune flag, target 4800 tris), recompute normals with 50 deg crease angle, then glTF-Transform optimize --simplify false (meshopt compression + quantization)

dimensionsMeters.pivot: base center (y = 0, XZ centered; node translation ~0.0001 m)
dimensionsMeters.footprintCells: 2 x 2 at native scale (4 x 4 m); 1 x 1 at scale 0.5 (1.96 m)

suggestedUses.use: focus_altar base (pedestal under the Focus Altar)
suggestedUses.result: 1.96 m diameter x 0.325 m tall, fits one 2 x 2 m cell; matches the single-cell, STONE, movement-blocking focus_altar object
3.92 m diameter x 0.65 m tall, covers a 2 x 2 cell block; not a walkable level (rules only know ground and 4 m platforms)

notes: `file` is the optimized derivative loaded by the game (4.8k triangles, ~72 KB). The 1.95M-triangle original lives in assets/models/source/environment/ and stays the high-poly reference. Regenerate with `npm run optimize-models -- plate`.
The glTF-Transform CLI simplify stalled at ~88k triangles because the original NORMAL attribute has seams that block edge collapses; dropping NORMAL before welding fixes it.
The optimized file uses EXT_meshopt_compression: Babylon.js needs the meshopt decoder (loaded from CDN by default; set MeshoptCompression.Configuration for offline use).
dimensionsMeters describes the original; the optimized bounds are within ~4 mm of it (base still at y = 0, top at 0.648 m).
No material, no UVs and no textures: renders with the engine default material. Assign a stone material in the loader; texturing requires UV unwrapping in a derived file.
Radially symmetric, so front (+Z) orientation is irrelevant.
Scale and any offset should be applied in the loader (root transform), not by editing the GLB.
